title: Bluey and the balloon game.
lines: She is six years old and she loves games.
She lives in a house with a big garden, with her little sister Bingo, her mum Chilli and her dad Bandit.
Bingo is four and she is orange.
He goes to the cupboard and comes back with a red balloon.
The balloon gets bigger and bigger.
Dad ties a knot in it.
This is the game, says Dad.
The balloon must not touch the ground.
Bluey jumps and taps it back.
Bingo runs and taps it up.
Dad dives over the sofa and taps it just in time.
The balloon goes higher and lower.
Dad does a funny jump and falls on the floor.
Bluey and Bingo laugh so hard that they almost forget the balloon.
The balloon floats into the kitchen.
With her wooden spoon she taps the balloon back.
The four of them run through the house.
The balloon floats down the hall, up the stairs, and down again.
It goes outside, through the open door, into the garden.
Outside there's a bit of wind.
The balloon floats towards the tree.
It almost gets caught on a branch.
Bingo climbs onto the swing and taps it away.
It floats towards the paddling pool.
Bluey jumps in, clothes and all.
But she taps the balloon up.
Then the neighbours come and look over the hedge.
asks Lucky, the puppy from next door.
Now there are five of them playing.
They count how many times they tap.
And then a gust of wind comes.
The balloon flies over the roof.
It floats away, high in the sky.
The balloon gets smaller and smaller.
A little red dot in the blue sky.
Dad sits down next to her.
And now the balloon is going on a journey.
Maybe it'll fly to the sea.
That evening, in bed, Bluey and Bingo are still talking about it.
Where do you think the balloon is now?
Maybe with the stars, whispers Bluey.
Dad pops in one more time.
He's holding something behind his back.
Tomorrow, he says, we'll play again.
And he shows them a little bag.
A yellow one, a green one, a blue one and a pink one.
And the floor isn't lava anymore.
